lines: Pick an open map, and Race Setup shows it, then asks whom you want to race.
The map's photo, its name and route, and three facts: distance, climbing and rating. Your best joins them once you have one.
Stars here lists the three rules. An earned one is struck through, and a screen reader hears earned.
On the map that holds your next unlock, a gold line names the goal: finish top three against bots here, to open Cliffside Coast.
Race against: your best time, bots, chosen by default, or riders online, locked until rider level three.
It's one radio group. The arrow keys move the choice, and pass over the locked one.
Against bots, pack strength sets their pace: easy, around a hundred and thirty watts; medium, one ninety; hard, two fifty.
Go to the start line opens the race with that pack. Your best time reads Start ride, and goes solo at once.
A locked map's address never shows its setup. It opens Map Select instead.
From a phone to a desktop, where the ride panel sits beside the map, with Start at its foot.
What the tests prove: nine behaviour specs, the planner's table and the catalogue through the API, all green, and the first bundle under budget.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
